title: RF-DETR vs YOLOv9: 58.6 vs 57.1 mAP, YOLOv9 21.6% faster
dek: RF-DETR-L tops out at 58.6 mAP, YOLOv9-C at 57.1. At matched size, YOLOv9 runs 21.6% faster on an RTX 5070 Ti and wins 3 of 5 pairs.
author: Vision Analysis

blocks.text: YOLOv9 is the stronger family per parameter on an RTX 5070 Ti: it wins 3 of 5 nearest-parameter pairs, averages 4.5 mAP points higher, and runs 21.6% faster in PyTorch. Read the average with care: every pair faces YOLOv9-C, and the segmentation variant RF-DETR-Seg-N, scores 40.4 mAP against 57.1 and drags the average on its own. RF-DETR-M and RF-DETR-L still beat YOLOv9-C, by 0.2 and 1.5 points, and RF-DETR-L reaches the higher ceiling at 58.6 mAP.

RF-DETR fields 5 measured variants; YOLOv9 fields 4. All run the same COCO val2017 protocol on an RTX 5070 Ti. RF-DETR's variants sit between 30.47M and 33.93M parameters, so each pairs with YOLOv9-C (25.5M) by count.

blocks.caption: Accuracy vs parameters on COCO val2017. Every RF-DETR and YOLOv9 variant highlighted against the full set.

blocks.text: mAP is shown in percent. Against YOLOv9-C at 57.1 mAP, RF-DETR-N trails at 51.4, RF-DETR-S at 55.1 and RF-DETR-Seg-N at 40.4. RF-DETR-M leads by 0.2 points at 57.3 and RF-DETR-L by 1.5 at 58.6. At the small end YOLOv9-T reaches 41.8 mAP at 2.04M parameters, a size class RF-DETR does not field; RF-DETR's smallest, RF-DETR-N, needs 30.47M for 51.4 mAP.
YOLOv9 is faster at matched compute: 21.6% faster on average in PyTorch FP32. YOLOv9-C runs 42.3 FPS; RF-DETR runs 39.5 FPS at RF-DETR-N and 25.1 FPS at RF-DETR-L.

items.v: Both families ship under permissive licenses

blocks.text: Pick YOLOv9 for small and mid-size deployments and for throughput: it fields models from 2.04M parameters and is faster at matched size. Pick RF-DETR-L when peak accuracy matters more than frame rate: it reaches 58.6 mAP, 1.5 points above YOLOv9-C, at 25.1 vs 42.3 FPS. Both ship under permissive licenses. See the per-variant specs on the RF-DETR and YOLOv9 model pages.
